def load_sim(nside, theta_pix, pol, master_seed, uk_arcmin_t = 3, H0 = None,
             ombh2 = 0.0224567, omch2 = 0.118489, cosmomc_theta = 0.0104098,
             r = 0.0, mnu = DEFAULT_MNU, tau = DEFAULT_TAUREIO, As = jnp.exp(3.043) * 1e-10,
             nt = 0, ns = 0.968602, lmax = 4000, begin_ell_interp = None, l_knee = 100,
             k_pivot = DEFAULT_K_PIVOT, Alens = DEFAULT_A_LENSE, nphi_fac = 2, a_phi = 1,
             precomputed_cls = None, max_l_tensor = DEFAULT_MAX_L_TENSOR,
             max_eta_k_tensor = DEFAULT_MAX_ETA_K_TENSOR, use_mask = False):
    """Simulate a lensed CMB data set on a flat nside x nside sky patch.

    Runs CAMB for the requested cosmology, builds the field, phi and noise covariances in
    Fourier space, draws the unlensed field(s), phi and the noise, lenses the field with
    LenseFlow and returns everything in one data set object. CAMB runs inside
    `jax.pure_callback`, so a CAMB failure gives NaN spectra rather than an exception.

    Randomness: one root key PRNGKey(master_seed), and every random field (phi, then the
    unlensed field(s), then the noise) splits its own subkey off it in that fixed order
    (field_from_covar). So the realization at a seed depends on the cosmology only through
    the covariances the white noise is scaled by.

    Args:
        nside: Number of pixels on a side.
        theta_pix: Pixel width in arcmin.
        pol: "I" (temperature only), "P" (E/B polarization only) or "IP" (both).
        master_seed: Root seed of every random draw.
        uk_arcmin_t: White noise level in temperature, in uK-arcmin. The polarization
            noise is sqrt(2) higher.
        H0: Hubble constant. Leave as None to set the expansion through `cosmomc_theta`.
        ombh2: Physical baryon density.
        omch2: Physical cold dark matter density.
        cosmomc_theta: CosmoMC's approximation to the angular size of the sound horizon
            (the sampler's theta_MC_100 divided by 100).
        r: Tensor-to-scalar ratio.
        mnu: Sum of the neutrino masses in eV.
        tau: Optical depth to reionization.
        As: Primordial scalar amplitude (the sampler's logA is log(1e10 As)).
        nt: Tensor spectral index.
        ns: Scalar spectral index.
        lmax: Largest multipole of the spectra.
        begin_ell_interp: Optional multipole past which the spectra are extrapolated
            rather than taken from CAMB.
        l_knee: Knee of the 1/f noise term. 0 gives pure white noise, as every sampler
            entry point uses.
        k_pivot: Pivot scale of the primordial spectra, in 1/Mpc.
        Alens: CAMB's lensing amplitude.
        nphi_fac: Factor the quadratic-estimate noise is divided by (CMBLensing.jl's
            preconditioning heuristic).
        a_phi: Amplitude multiplying the phi covariance.
        precomputed_cls: Optional dict of CAMB spectra to use instead of running CAMB, for
            callers that build many realizations at one cosmology. It must be in
            `_extract_all_cls`'s format (e.g. the output of
            `fisher_forecast.camb_cls_at_params`) and must belong to the same cosmology as
            the keyword arguments, which are then unused.
        max_l_tensor: CAMB's largest multipole for the tensor spectra.
        max_eta_k_tensor: CAMB's largest k * eta for the tensor spectra.
        use_mask: Apply a sky mask. False (the default) uses a mask of all ones.

    Returns:
        A `DataSetT` (pol = "I"), `DataSetEB` (pol = "P") or `DataSetTEB` (pol = "IP")
        holding the fields (`unlensed_field`, `lensed_field`, `phi`, `data`) and the
        operators (`field_covariance`, `phi_covariance`, `noise_covariance`, `mask`,
        `beam`, `mixing_d`, `mixing_g`, `quadratic_estimate`, ...). All fields are in
        Fourier space.

    Example:
        ```python
        from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
        data_set = load_sim(nside = 128, theta_pix = 2.5, pol = "IP", master_seed = 67,
                            uk_arcmin_t = 5, l_knee = 0)
        ```
    """

    lmax_prime = min(lmax, DEFAULT_MAX_ELL) if begin_ell_interp is None else min(lmax, begin_ell_interp)

    if precomputed_cls is None:
        unlensed_scalar, tensor, total, lens_potential = _camb_via_callback(
            H0, ombh2, omch2, cosmomc_theta, r, mnu, tau, As, nt, ns,
            lmax_prime, k_pivot, Alens, max_l_tensor, max_eta_k_tensor
        )
        cls = _extract_all_cls(unlensed_scalar, tensor, total, lens_potential, lmax, lmax_prime)
    else:
        cls = _validate_precomputed_cls(precomputed_cls, lmax)

    ell_grid, pix_width = gen_ell_grid(nside, theta_pix)
    #one root key; every draw below splits its own subkey off it (field_from_covar). The draw
    #ORDER (phi, the field(s), the noise) is fixed and independent of the cosmology, so two
    #calls at the same seed share every white-noise realization - the common random numbers
    #delensed_covariance.py's stencil relies on
    rng_key = jax.random.PRNGKey(master_seed)
    ells = jnp.arange(2, lmax).astype(jnp.float64)

    #ells arrays matched to the cls lengths: the emulator override returns ells
    #2..lmax inclusive while the CAMB dl2cl path returns 2..lmax-1
    phi_ells = jnp.arange(2, 2 + cls["phi"].shape[0]).astype(jnp.float64)

    #Lensing potential
    unscaled_cphi = covar_matrix_from_cls(nside, pix_width, ell_grid,
                                          phi_ells,
                                          cls["phi"], origin_value=0)
    cphi = a_phi * unscaled_cphi
    phi, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cphi, rng_key)

    #Unlensed field covariances (scalar + tensor). Unlensed scalar BB (identically zero
    #at r = 0) cannot go through the log-interpolating covariance builder (log(0) -> NaN)
    #so _covar_or_zeros maps it to an exactly zero matrix. TE crosses zero, so it is
    #built from the correlation ratio rho = Cl_TE / sqrt(Cl_TT * Cl_EE) instead
    #(te_covar_from_rho): linear interpolation of rho onto the ell grid, scaled by
    #sqrt(cf_tt * cf_ee), which keeps the T/E block positive semi-definite by
    #construction and matched to the sampler's grid-spline TE path
    cf = {}
    cf_scalar = {}
    cf_tensor = {}
    pol_comps = ("TT",) if pol == "I" else ("TT", "EE", "BB")
    for comp in pol_comps:
        scalar_ells = jnp.arange(2, 2 + cls[f"scalar_{comp}"].shape[0]).astype(jnp.float64)
        cf_scalar[comp] = _covar_or_zeros(nside, pix_width, ell_grid,
                                          scalar_ells,
                                          cls[f"scalar_{comp}"], origin_value=0)
        cf_tensor[comp] = _covar_or_zeros(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, ells,
                                          cls[f"tensor_{comp}"], origin_value=0)
        cf[comp] = cf_scalar[comp] + cf_tensor[comp]
    if pol != "I":
        scalar_ells = jnp.arange(2, 2 + cls["scalar_TE"].shape[0]).astype(jnp.float64)
        rho_te = te_rho_from_cls(cls["scalar_TE"], cls["scalar_TT"], cls["scalar_EE"])
        cf["TE"] = cf_scalar["TE"] = te_covar_from_rho(rho_te, scalar_ells, ell_grid,
                                                       cf["TT"], cf["EE"])
        cf_tensor["TE"] = jnp.zeros((nside, nside // 2 + 1))

    #Lensed field covariances (TE via the same correlation-ratio route)
    cfl = {comp: covar_matrix_from_cls(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, ells,
                                       cls[f"total_{comp}"], origin_value=0)
           for comp in ("TT", "EE", "BB")}
    rho_te_lensed = te_rho_from_cls(cls["total_TE"], cls["total_TT"], cls["total_EE"])
    cfl["TE"] = te_covar_from_rho(rho_te_lensed, ells, ell_grid, cfl["TT"], cfl["EE"])

    #Unlensed random fields. T and E are drawn CORRELATED to match the model's TE block:
    #E ~ N(0, C_EE), then T = (C_TE / C_EE) E + t_indep with
    #t_indep ~ N(0, C_TT - C_TE^2 / C_EE), which gives exactly
    #Cov = [[C_TT, C_TE], [C_TE, C_EE]] (the conditional variance is
    #C_TT (1 - rho^2) >= 0 by the |rho| <= 1 construction; the maximum(0) guards
    #round-off only). The B draw against a zero covariance gives an exactly zero field
    if pol == "I":
        field_t, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cf["TT"], rng_key)
    else:
        conditional_tt = jnp.maximum(
            cf["TT"] - cf["TE"]**2 * reciprocal_matrix(cf["EE"]), 0.0)
        t_indep, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, conditional_tt, rng_key)
        field_e, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cf["EE"], rng_key)
        field_b, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cf["BB"], rng_key)
        te_ratio = cf["TE"] * reciprocal_matrix(cf["EE"])
        field_t = jfft.irfft2(te_ratio * jfft.rfft2(field_e)) + t_indep

    #Lensing
    if pol == "I":
        lensed_t = jfft.rfft2(primal_lense_flow(
            field_t, phi, pix_width, n=10, direction=FORWARD_LENSE, adjoint=False
        ))
    else:
        lensed_t, lensed_e, lensed_b = _lens_fields(
            field_t, field_e, field_b, phi, pix_width, nside, theta_pix
        )

    beam = get_beam(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, lmax_prime)
    #NOTE we have removed the mask for LCDM inference
    mask = get_mask(DEFAULT_MASK_ELL, nside, pix_width, ell_grid) if use_mask else jnp.ones_like(beam)

    #Noise covariance and white noise (the TE noise Cls are identically zero, so
    #_covar_or_zeros keeps that block an exact zero matrix instead of NaN)
    n_tt, n_te, n_ee, n_bb = noise_cls(lmax_prime, uk_arcmin_t, l_knee = l_knee)
    ell_prime = jnp.arange(2, lmax_prime)
    cn = {}
    for comp, ncl in zip(("TT", "TE", "EE", "BB"), (n_tt, n_te, n_ee, n_bb)):
        cn[comp] = _covar_or_zeros(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, ell_prime, ncl, origin_value=0)

    wn_t, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cn["TT"], rng_key)
    if pol != "I":
        wn_e, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cn["EE"], rng_key)
        wn_b, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cn["BB"], rng_key)

    #Data = Mask * Beam * Lensed + Noise
    data_t = mask * beam * lensed_t + jfft.rfft2(wn_t)
    if pol != "I":
        data_e = mask * beam * lensed_e + jfft.rfft2(wn_e)
        data_b = mask * beam * lensed_b + jfft.rfft2(wn_b)

    #Convert unlensed fields to Fourier space
    field_t = jfft.rfft2(field_t)
    if pol != "I":
        field_e, field_b = jfft.rfft2(field_e), jfft.rfft2(field_b)

    #D matrix (full T/E block including TE; see get_d_teb_matrix for the identity B
    #block at r = 0)
    d_tt = get_d_tt_matrix(cf["TT"], cn["TT"])
    if pol != "I":
        d_tt, d_te, d_ee, d_bb = get_d_teb_matrix(cf["TT"], cf["TE"], cf["EE"], cf["BB"],
                                                  cn["TT"], cn["TE"], cn["EE"], cn["BB"])

    #Quadratic estimate
    if pol == "I":
        qe = scalar_quadratic_estimate(cn["TT"], cf["TT"], cfl["TT"],
                                       mask, beam, pix_width) / nphi_fac
    else:
        qe = polar_quadratic_estimate(cf["EE"], cf["BB"], cfl["EE"], cfl["BB"],
                                      cn["EE"], cn["BB"], mask, mask,
                                      beam, beam, pix_width) / nphi_fac

    #The G mixing matrix    
    g = get_g_matrix(cphi, qe, a_phi, a_phi = a_phi)

    #convert phi back to fourier space
    phi = jfft.rfft2(phi)
    #Build dataset for the requested polarization
    if pol == "I":
        return _build_dataset_t(
            nside, theta_pix, pix_width, cphi, unscaled_cphi, qe, phi,
            cf, cf_scalar, cf_tensor, cfl, cn, d_tt, g, mask, beam,
            field_t, lensed_t, data_t, r, a_phi
        )
    elif pol == "P":
        return _build_dataset_eb(
            nside, theta_pix, pix_width, cphi, unscaled_cphi, qe, phi,
            cf, cf_scalar, cf_tensor, cfl, cn, d_ee, d_bb, g, mask, beam,
            field_e, field_b, lensed_e, lensed_b, data_e, data_b, r, a_phi
        )
    else:
        return _build_dataset_teb(
            nside, theta_pix, pix_width, cphi, unscaled_cphi, qe, phi,
            cf, cf_scalar, cf_tensor, cfl, cn, d_tt, d_te, d_ee, d_bb, g, mask, beam,
            field_t, field_e, field_b,
            lensed_t, lensed_e, lensed_b,
            data_t, data_e, data_b, r, a_phi
        )

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Maps live on a flat, periodic nside x nside box with theta_pix arcminutes per pixel. Three field types (cmb_lensing/fields.py) cover the polarization modes:

Type Content Arrays FlatS0 a scalar map (e.g. temperature or lensing potential) scalar_matrix FlatS2 polarization (E/B - Modes or Q/U - Modes) polar_matrix_1, polar_matrix_2 FlatS02 temperature + polarization scalar_matrix, polar_matrix_1, polar_matrix_2

A field carries a basis: either MAP (real space, (nside, nside), float64) or FOURIER (the rfft2 half plane, (nside, nside//2 + 1) complex128). Polarization is implicitly in either the EB or the QU parametrization. The conversions are

field = map(field)        #FOURIER -> MAP (irfft2)
field = fourier(field)    #MAP -> FOURIER (rfft2)
field = eb2qu(field)      #EB -> QU (in Fourier)
field = qu2eb(field)      #QU -> EB (in Fourier)

lense_flow takes fields in MAP / QU. Most other code works in FOURIER / EB.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Diagonal-in-Fourier operators (covariances, beam, mask, the mixing matrices) are in cmb_lensing/matrix_operators.py:

Type Used for DiagonalScalar T-only, and every phi operator DiagonalEB E/B operators BlockTEB T/E/B operators with a 2x2 T/E block (TT, TE, ET, EE, BB)

Arithmetic is element-wise per block, except BlockTEB multiplication, which is the 2x2 T/E matrix product. pinv and log_det dispatch on the operator type.

Fields and operators are flax.struct.dataclass pytrees, so they pass through jax.jit, jax.grad and jax.vmap directly.

docs.title: Polarization modes
docs.text:
pol selects the configuration everywhere (load_sim, map_joint, sample_joint):

pol Fields Operators Data set "I" FlatS0 DiagonalScalar DataSetT "P" FlatS2 DiagonalEB DataSetEB "IP" FlatS02 BlockTEB DataSetTEB

docs.title: Simulating Data
docs.text:
cmb_lensing.simulate.load_sim is the main entry point. It

  1. runs CAMB for the requested cosmology,
  2. builds the field, phi and noise covariances in Fourier space,
  3. draws the unlensed field, phi and the noise,
  4. lenses the field with primal_lense_flow,
  5. returns a DataSetT / DataSetEB / DataSetTEB holding the fields, the operators and the simulated data.
from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
data_set = load_sim(nside = 128,         #pixels per side
                    theta_pix = 2.5,     #arcmin per pixel
                    pol = "IP",          #"I", "P" or "IP"
                    master_seed = 67,
                    uk_arcmin_t = 5,     #white noise level in T (P is sqrt(2) higher)
                    l_knee = 0)          #0 for pure white noise

Useful attributes of the returned data set: unlensed_field, lensed_field, phi, data, field_covariance, phi_covariance, noise_covariance, mask, beam, mixing_d, mixing_g, quadratic_estimate.

docs.title: Choices to know about
docs.text:
• Noise sprectra are computed via noise_cls(...) with a 1/f term. The defaults are l_knee = 100 and alpha_knee = 3. The default beam FWHM is 0.
  • Cosmology is given in CAMB's names (cosmomc_theta, As, ombh2, omch2, ns, ...). The sampler's names (theta_MC_100, logA) are converted by to_camb_naming_conv (which edits its dict in place) or fisher_forecast.load_sim_cosmology.
  • CAMB runs inside jax.pure_callback, so load_sim is traceable. A CAMB failure gives NaN spectra and a non-finite logpdf, never an exception.

docs.title: MAP Estimation
docs.text:
map_joint(data_set, num_steps = 30, constant_step = False) (cmb_lensing/map_joint.py) finds the joint maximum a posteriori (f, phi) given the data, following Millea et al. 2017. The objective is

\[ -2 \log P(f, \phi \mid d) = \frac{(d - M B L(\phi) f)^2}{C_n} + \frac{f^2}{C_f} + \frac{\phi^2}{C_\phi} + \text{const.} \]

Each step alternates

  1. a Wiener filter for f at the current phi, and
  2. a BFGS line search on phi along the preconditioned mixed gradient (mixed_grad_phi_logpdf), with Hessian approximation pinv(Cphi^-1 + Nphi^-1).

The G mixing matrix is set to the identity (the MAP is invariant to it).

from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
from cmb_lensing.map_joint import map_joint

data_set = load_sim(nside = 128, theta_pix = 2.5, pol = "I", master_seed = 67, uk_arcmin_t = 5)
field_predict, phi_predict = map_joint(data_set, num_steps = 30)

A full worked example, with plots of the lensing, inverse lensing, logpdf and the cross spectra of the reconstruction against the truth, can be found in the map_joint tutorial notebook.

docs.title: LCDM Sampling (sample_joint)
docs.text:
sample_joint (cmb_lensing/sample_lcdm.py) draws samples from the joint posterior \(P(f, \phi, \theta \mid d)\) by Gibbs sampling, where theta are the five LCDM parameters

PARAM_ORDER = ["theta_MC_100", "logA", "ns", "ombh2", "omch2"]

The optical depth to reionization tau is fixed at 0.05 and the neutrino mass mnu at 0.06. The fiducial values, the ±5-sigma search box and the parameter scales are GROUND_TRUTH, PARAM_BOUNDS and PARAM_SIGMA in cmb_lensing/constants.py.

docs.title: One Gibbs iteration
docs.text:
The structure mirrors CMBLensing.jl's sample_joint:

  1. f step (gibbs_sample_f): draw f from its conditional with a simulated realization plus a Wiener-filter correction.
  2. mix: change to the mixed parametrization \(f^\circ = L(\phi) \cdot D \cdot f\); \(\text{ }\phi^\circ = G \cdot\phi\) following Millea, et. al. 2020.
  3. phi step (gibbs_sample_phi): one HMC step on the mixed phi field with mass matrix given by \(G^{-2}(C_\phi^{-1} + N_\phi^{-1})\).
  4. theta step: for each sampled parameter, a Gaussian random-walk Metropolis move of width proposal_sigmas[name] on the mixed logpdf. Proposals outside param_ranges[name] or outside the CAMB grid are rejected.
  5. update \(C_\mathrm{\phi}\), \(C_f\), \(D\), \(G\) at the accepted theta.
  6. unmix back to (f, phi) with the updated D and G.

The theta step is skipped for the first num_burn_in_fix_theta iterations.

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
Before a large experiment, run a pilot chain by calling the __main__ method of sample_lcdm.py on a small map and tune

  • proposal_sigmas toward ~44 % acceptance per parameter,
  • hmc_step_size / hmc_num_steps toward ~65 % phi acceptance.

advanced_logging = {"phi_acceptance": True, "lcdm_acceptance": True, ...} prints the running rates. plot_log_pdf / plot_lcdm_sigmas write progress plots to cmb_lensing/sample_lcdm_output/, which must exist first.

See the sample_joint tutorial for a worked example, and LCDM Sampling on the HPC for running many chains in parallel.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: sample_joint returns (param_vals, phi, sub_key): a dict of per-parameter lists, the final phi and the final random key. With hpc_path set, every iteration appends the latest value of each sampled parameter to {hpc_path}{theta}_map_{map_idx}_chain_{sub_chain_idx}_history.txt, which cmb_lensing/chain_analysis.py (see Chain Analysis) reads and analyzes to form distributions out of the sampled data.

docs.title: The CAMB Grid
docs.text:
sample_joint needs the theory power spectra at every proposed LCDM parameter combination. It gets them from a precomputed grid of real CAMB spectra: a 5D tensor-product cubic spline over (H0, logA, ns, ombh2, omch2), stored in camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz (~7.9 GB). It serves any subset of the five parameters and every polarization mode.

The file is fetched automatically from the Hugging Face dataset the first time it is needed (or ahead of time with cmb-lensing-download-splines, see Installation). To use your own grid instead, rebuild it on the cluster using the slurm scripts in /camb_grid_generation, SCP it back to your local machine and place it at camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text: The grid is opened once per process and each spectrum's spline is built lazily on first use (~2.1 GB resident per spectrum). Temperature-only sampling loads TT + PP (~4.5 GB); pol = "IP" loads TT / EE / TE / PP (~9.1 GB).

docs.title: Validating the grid
docs.text:
python tests/test_camb_grid.py --grid camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz -n 20

compares the spline against direct CAMB at random interior points. Typical max |Δ ln Cl| is ~1e-3 (TT) to ~5e-3 (EE, near an acoustic trough).

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
The repository's large data is too big for GitHub. All of it is stored on the Hugging Face dataset zaneblood1/cmb_lensing_data (~23 GB). The dataset card there describes every file format.

Dataset path Size Contents Written by camb_grid_spline.npz 7.9 GB the 5D CAMB grid (The CAMB Grid) camb_grid_generation/ joint_inference_data/ 512 MB LCDM chains, one folder per run get_lcdm_samples/ (LCDM Sampling on the HPC) delensed_field_covariance_data/ 683 MB empirical delensed covariances get_delensed_field_covariance/ (Delensed Covariances) map_joint_phi_noise_data/ 98 MB map_joint's per-mode N_phi measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/ (MAP Joint Phi Noise) sampler_phi_noise_data/ 787 MB the sampler's per-mode N_phi measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise/ (Sampler Phi Noise) map_joint_comparison/ 13 GB map_joint timings and reconstructions, Python vs Julia runtime_comparison/

docs.title: Downloading
docs.text:
Only the CAMB grid is downloaded automatically (Installation). Fetch anything else with the hf command that huggingface_hub installs, one folder at a time:

hf download zaneblood1/cmb_lensing_data --repo-type dataset \
    --include "joint_inference_data/*" --local-dir cmb_lensing_data

Drop the --include to download everything.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
Nothing in the package looks for these folders at a fixed location: every script takes the path of the file or folder it reads.

#chain analysis of one run, with the forecast
python -m cmb_lensing.chain_analysis cmb_lensing_data/joint_inference_data/joint_inference_2026_10_29_2.5uk \
    --nside 128 --theta_pix 2.5 --noise 2.5 --run_fisher \
    --delensed_covariance cmb_lensing_data/delensed_field_covariance_data/delensed_covariance_output_map_joint_2.5uk/delensed_covariance.npz \
    --phi_noise cmb_lensing_data/map_joint_phi_noise_data/map_joint_phi_noise_output_2.5uk/map_joint_phi_noise.npz

#the forecast on its own
python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 \
    --delensed_covariance cmb_lensing_data/delensed_field_covariance_data/delensed_covariance_output_map_joint_5uk/delensed_covariance.npz

See Chain Analysis and Fisher Forecast for the options. The map_joint comparison figures are remade by runtime_comparison/performance_analysis.py, with the BASE_DIR / RESULTS_DIR at its top pointed at the downloaded map_joint_comparison/performance_results folder.

docs.title: HPC Setup
docs.text: All cluster scripts are Slurm scripts. Before running any of them, create hpc_local.sh at the repository root as described in Installation.

docs.title: How the drivers work
docs.text:
Each pipeline folder has a driver that only submits jobs, and is run with bash, not sbatch:

bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh

A driver can be run from any directory. It cds into its own folder, sources the repo-root hpc_local.sh and hpc_submit.sh (../, or ../../ from inside measure_phi_noise/) and submits its job script once per job. Job scripts find their Python file and hpc_local.sh through $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR, and write their output inside the driver's folder, so the checkout can live anywhere.

docs.title: Submission throttle
docs.text:
Some clusters (ACES among them) cancel every submission beyond a cap on queued jobs instead of leaving it pending. Every driver therefore submits through submit_throttled (repo-root hpc_submit.sh): before each sbatch it waits until you have fewer than MAX_QUEUED_JOBS jobs queued or running (default 85), checking every SUBMIT_POLL_SECONDS (default 60), and it retries a rejected sbatch. Override either value in hpc_local.sh.

A driver now runs until its last job is submitted, which can take hours. Keep it alive after you log out:

nohup bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh > submit.log 2>&1 &
tail -f submit.log

nohup ignores the hangup signal sent at logout, > submit.log 2>&1 sends output and errors to the file, and & runs it in the background. Alternatively run the driver inside tmux, detach with Ctrl-b d, and reattach later with tmux attach (on the same login node).

The physical configuration (nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, ...) is set by editing variables at the top of each driver. Keep them the same across drivers for one experiment, so the chains, the phi-noise measurements and the forecasts all describe the same box.

Driver Output folder camb_grid_generation/camb_grid.sh camb_grid_generation/multi_param_CAMB_grid/ get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh get_lcdm_samples/lcdm_sampler_data/<experiment>/ measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise.sh measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/map_joint_phi_noise_output/ measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise.sh measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise/sampler_phi_noise_output/ get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh get_delensed_field_covariance/delensed_covariance_output/ runtime_comparison/run_performance_test.sh runtime_comparison/performance_results/

Every driver's settings are defaults that can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value> (quote a list, e.g. --map_sizes="128 256"); the folder name is --out_dir_name. Each run writes the submission date and every setting to submission_settings.txt in its output folder, replacing any earlier copy.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install it in editable mode from the repository root (the folder holding pyproject.toml):

git clone https://github.com/zaneblood1/CMBLensing.py.git
cd CMBLensing.py
pip install -e .

This pulls in JAX (pinned to jax == jaxlib == 0.9.2), Flax, CAMB, NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib. Python 3.10 or newer is required. JAX is configured for float64 globally on import.

Optional extras:

pip install -e ".[dev]"    #pytest + jupyter
pip install -e ".[docs]"   #MkDocs, to build this site locally

docs.title: Check the install
docs.text:
from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
data_set = load_sim(nside = 64, theta_pix = 5, pol = "I", master_seed = 1)
print(f"Pixel resolution = {data_set.theta_pix} arcminutes per pixel")

If you wish to run the unit tests or actively contribute to the development of the repository it will also be necessary to have juliacall installed and a CMBLensing.jl checkout - see Testing for more information.

docs.title: Downloading the 5D CAMB grid
docs.text:
sample_joint evaluates its theory spectra through a 5D CAMB spline, camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz (~7.9 GB). This file is too large to store on GitHub. It is hosted on the Hugging Face dataset zaneblood1/cmb_lensing_data and is downloaded automatically into camb_splines/ the first time the code needs it (cmb_lensing/camb_splines.py). No manual step is needed.

To fetch it ahead of time, run

cmb-lensing-download-splines

On a cluster, run this once on a login node: compute nodes often have no internet access. You can also rebuild the grid yourself (Building the CAMB Grid) and place it at camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz. See The CAMB Grid for more information on how the grid is used.

The same dataset holds the chains, phi noise, delensed covariance and map_joint comparison outputs. None of those is downloaded automatically; see Data.

docs.title: HPC setup (hpc_local.sh)
docs.text:
If you wish to run any of the HPC slurm scripts for e.g. sampling LCDM parameters en masse or generating data for Fisher forecasting, you will need to make a copy of the hpc_local.example.sh script and fill it in with your own personal cluster configurations. The example script is gitignored to avoid sharing personal email accounts, etc.

cp hpc_local.example.sh hpc_local.sh

then edit hpc_local.sh:

#the conda install and environment the jobs run in
source /path/to/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate myenv

#where Slurm mails job failures
export SBATCH_MAIL_USER=you@example.edu

#the CMBLensing.jl checkout, used only by runtime_comparison/
export CMBLENSING_JL_PATH=/path/to/CMBLensing.jl

Every driver and every job script it submits sources this file. See HPC setup for how the drivers work.

docs.title: Building these docs locally
docs.text:
mkdocs serve      #live-reloading preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build      #static site in site/

docs.title: Building the CAMB Grid
docs.text: Most users should download the grid. Rebuild it when CAMB is upgraded or the grid's box changes.

docs.title: The 5D grid
docs.text:
The 5D spline is used to interpolate real CAMB spectra on a tensor-product grid over (H0, logA, ns, ombh2, omch2) with (tau = 0.05, mnu = 0.06, r = 0), evaluated in log spectra space (cmb_lensing/camb_grid_interp.py). The grid is laid out in H0 because a rectangular box in theta_MC_100 has corners CAMB cannot solve; the sampler works in theta_MC_100 and converts back and forth through a stored theta(H0, ombh2, omch2) table.

cd camb_grid_generation
bash camb_grid.sh                                            #875 jobs, one 81-point H0 sweep each
python merge_camb_grid.py --grid_dir multi_param_CAMB_grid   #-> multi_param_CAMB_grid/camb_grid_spline.npz
python ../tests/test_camb_grid.py --grid multi_param_CAMB_grid/camb_grid_spline.npz -n 20

Every grid setting has a default in camb_grid.sh and can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value>: the CAMB settings (lmax, tau, mnu, k_pivot, alens, accuracy_boost, l_sample_boost, l_accuracy_boost), the output folder's name inside camb_grid_generation/ (out_dir_name), each axis range (h0_min / h0_max, log_a_*, ns_*, ombh2_*, omch2_*) and the nodes per axis (h0_nodes, log_a_nodes, ns_nodes, ombh2_nodes, omch2_nodes). For example

bash camb_grid.sh --lmax=5000 --h0_nodes=101 --out_dir_name=grid_lmax_5000

A misspelled name is not an error: it is simply ignored and the default is used. Every run writes the submission date and all setting values to submission_settings.txt in the output folder (replacing any earlier copy), so check that file to see what a grid was built with. Use a new out_dir_name when you change settings.

Point merge_camb_grid.py --grid_dir at the folder you named.

Regenerating the grid on an cluster will result in 81 x 5 x 5 x 5 x 7 = 70_875 CAMB calls in total. The jobs need only numpy and CAMB. The merge splines one spectrum at a time, in ell chunks, so the tables are never all in memory. Move the result to camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz (a file already there is used as is, never re-downloaded). If the new grid should replace the shared one, upload it to the Hugging Face dataset and tell everyone to delete their local copy.

docs.title: Chain Analysis
docs.text:
python -m cmb_lensing.chain_analysis <chain_dir> --nside 128 --theta_pix 2.5 --noise 2.5

turns a directory of LCDM chains into MCMC plots and, on request, compares them with one Fisher forecast. The tutorial notebook walks through it on data in the repository, and the Python entry points are in the API reference.

<chain_dir> holds the <param>_map_<seed>_chain_<index>_history.txt files that sample_joint writes. The sampled parameters, the maps and their sub-chains are read off the file names. The analysis does not depend on which data the chains saw, so it works for temperature (--pol I), polarization (P) and joint (IP) runs; --pol labels the plots and tells the forecast which data to model.

docs.title: What it computes
docs.text:
• Per-parameter diagnostics: the Gelman-Rubin R-hat across each map's sub-chains, the Metropolis acceptance rate, autocorrelations and integrated autocorrelation times.
  • Per-parameter plots, each sub-chain thinned by its integrated autocorrelation time: traces, per-map marginals and the histogram of per-map means.
  • The product distribution (the renormalized product of the per-map KDEs) and z_scores.png. The table is written in standard notation: 0.1092(1) means 0.1092 ± 0.0001. The product mean, product std and z-score, (truth − product mean) / product std, carry Monte Carlo errors from a bootstrap. Each of the N_BOOTSTRAP replicates resamples every map's thinned chain with replacement, keeping its length, then rebuilds the product and forms its z-score. The average single-map std carries the std of the per-map widths / sqrt(number of maps).
  • The chains' covariance: one np.cov per map (its unthinned sub-chains concatenated), averaged over maps, with a delete-one-map jackknife error.
  • Optionally one forecast (--run_fisher), compared with the chains. Forecasts carry no error bars.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --nside, --theta_pix, --noise 128, 2.5, 2.5 the box the chains ran on (pixels per side, arcmin, uK-arcmin); they label the triangle plot and set the forecast's box --pol I I, P or IP: the data the chains saw --burn_in 1000 sweeps removed from the start of every sub-chain --no_thin off skip the thinning before the per-parameter plots --out_dir <chain_dir>/chain_analysis_output where the plots go --run_fisher off also run the forecast and compare it with the chains --delensed_covariance none a merged delensed_covariance.npz; required by --run_fisher --qe_filter unlensed unlensed or lensed: the spectra in the filter of the forecast's QE N0 --phi_noise none a merged map_joint_phi_noise.npz or sampler_phi_noise.npz; its nphi replaces the QE N0 --no_bb off for P / IP chains: leave the delensed BB block out of the forecast --camb_lmax 4000 how far the forecast runs CAMB

docs.title: The forecast
docs.text:
The forecast does not run unless --run_fisher is given. It is the Fisher forecast for the chains' --pol, with white noise and no beam.

  • Field blocks: always the empirical delensed covariance of --delensed_covariance, measured at the chains' box, noise level and --pol. Without the file --run_fisher is an error; there is no analytic delensing fallback.
  • Phi noise: by default the box quadratic-estimate N0, built like load_sim's (without its NPHI_FAC; the TT estimator for I, the EB estimator for P and IP), with the unlensed spectra in both the response and the filter. --qe_filter lensed puts the lensed spectra in the filter; the response is always unlensed. --phi_noise replaces the N0 with a measured per-mode matrix.
  • BB: for P and IP the delensed BB block is counted unless --no_bb is given.

Build the delensed covariance's Wiener filter from the same N_phi the forecast uses.

python -m cmb_lensing.chain_analysis <chain_dir> --noise 2.5 --run_fisher \
    --delensed_covariance <delensed_covariance.npz>                          #unlensed QE N0
python -m cmb_lensing.chain_analysis <chain_dir> --noise 2.5 --run_fisher \
    --delensed_covariance <delensed_covariance.npz> --qe_filter lensed       #lensed filter
python -m cmb_lensing.chain_analysis <chain_dir> --noise 2.5 --run_fisher \
    --delensed_covariance <delensed_covariance.npz> --phi_noise <map_joint_phi_noise.npz>

docs.title: Output Folder
docs.text:
<chain_dir>/chain_analysis_output/ (or --out_dir), overwritten by every run:

  • <param>/, one folder per sampled parameter
  • joint_information/: z_scores.png, triangle_plot.png, covariance_matrix_empirical.png, correlation_matrix_empirical.png; with --run_fisher also covariance_matrix_fisher.png, correlation_matrix_fisher.png, covariance_ratio_fisher_over_empirical.png and correlation_ratio_fisher_over_empirical.png

The phi-noise spectra plots are made separately by measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_analysis.py (see Sampler Phi Noise).

docs.title: Delensed Covariance
docs.text:
Measures the empirical per-mode covariance of the delensed field, and its finite difference in theta. It is the field block of the Fisher forecast, which cannot run without it.

Each job uses one seed and runs at every stencil point \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_0 \pm h_i\):

  1. load_sim(theta) at the chosen pol (common random numbers: at one seed the fields differ only through the cosmology),
  2. inverse-lens the noiseless lensed field by the Wiener-filtered true phi \(W\phi\), with \(W = C_\phi / (C_\phi + N_\phi)\) built once at \(\theta_0\),
  3. store the per-mode covariance \(\mathrm{Re}(X Y^*) / n_\text{side}^2\) of every component on the rfft grid.
pol Stored components I TT P EE, BB IP TT, TE, EE, BB

The merge is the realization mean at each stencil point.

docs.title: Choosing N_phi for the Wiener Filter
docs.text:
Driver Setting What it Controls phi_noise="", qe_filter=unlensed (default) or lensed the box quadratic-estimate \(N^{(0)}\) (the TT estimator for I, the EB estimator for P and IP), with the unlensed or lensed spectra in its filter; the response is always unlensed phi_noise=<path> the nphi of a merged map_joint or sampler phi-noise file

Match it to the forecast it will feed: nothing checks that the file's W was built from the same N_phi as the forecast's phi block.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
bash get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh
#copy delensed_covariance_output/ to your machine, then
python get_delensed_field_covariance/merge_delensed_field_covariance.py --covariance_dir <delensed_covariance_output>

Other settings in the driver: pol (I, P or IP; the forecast must use the same), derivative_params (the forecast's --params must be drawn from this list), step_sigma (0.05, in units of PARAM_SIGMA; accurate at nside 128 / 2.5' / 2.5 to 10 uK-arcmin, so for another box or noise level rerun with the step halved and check that the forecast does not change substantially), num_realizations, seed_prefix, out_dir_name (the output folder's name inside get_delensed_field_covariance/). A 3-point temperature job at nside 128 takes ~20 s.

Every setting has a default in the driver and can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value>, e.g.

bash get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh --noise_level=10 --pol=IP \
    --derivative_params="omch2 logA" --out_dir_name=delensed_covariance_output_IP_10uk

A misspelled name is ignored and the default used. Each run writes the submission date and every setting to submission_settings.txt in the output folder (replacing any earlier copy); use a new out_dir_name when you change settings.

docs.title: Output: delensed_covariance.npz
docs.text:
Key Content pol, components the data's polarization and the stored components, in order delensed_fid the delensed covariance at \(\theta_0\), shape (n_components, nside, nside // 2 + 1) delensed_plus, delensed_minus the same at \(\theta_0 \pm h_i\), shape (n_params, n_components, nside, nside // 2 + 1) names, steps the differentiated parameters (in the package's standard order) and their steps \(h_i\) metadata the box, the stencil points, the seeds and how W was built

Merged temperature files written before 2026-11-11 have no components key and no component axis; the forecast still reads them.

docs.title: LCDM Sampling on the HPC
docs.text:
bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh

submits run_single_lcdm_chain.sh once per (data map, chain). Specify num_maps data realizations and num_chains chains per map in the master slurm submission script sample_lcdm.sh. Averaging over maps removes the cosmic variance of any one map, and running several chains per map checks convergence.

docs.title: What to set in sample_lcdm.sh
docs.text:
Variables Meaning nside, theta_pix, noise_level, pol basic configurations like pixel resolution, map size, etc, *_ground the ground-truth cosmology the data are simulated at *_min, *_max the sampling range for each parameter (by default ±5 sigma) num_maps, num_chains, map_prefix how many realizations and chains; map seeds are map_prefix * map sample_* true / false: whether each parameter is sampled (default omch2, theta_MC_100, logA). A sampled parameter starts each chain at a uniform random point in its [*_min, *_max] box, an unsampled one is held at *_ground *_proposal_sigma the Metropolis proposal width of each parameter (ombh2, omch2, theta_MC_100, log_a, ns) num_burn_in_fix_theta, iters_per_chain, num_burn_in_always_accept, hmc_num_steps, hmc_step_size sampler settings out_dir_name the run's folder inside lcdm_sampler_data/ (default joint_inference_<submission date>)

Every variable has a default in the script and can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value>, e.g.

bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh --noise_level=10 --omch2_proposal_sigma=2e-3 --out_dir_name=run_10uk

A misspelled name is ignored and the default used. Tune the proposal widths first with a pilot chain.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Chains are written as *_history.txt files (one line per iteration, every parameter) under get_lcdm_samples/lcdm_sampler_data/<out_dir_name>/. The same folder holds submission_settings.txt: the submission date, every setting, and each chain's random starting point (rewritten on every run, so use a new out_dir_name when you change settings). Copy that folder to your machine and run the chain analysis script.

docs.title: MAP Joint Phi Noise
docs.text:
Measures the per-mode reconstruction noise of map_joint at GROUND_TRUTH. Each job simulates one realization with load_sim, reconstructs phi with map_joint, and stores per rfft2 mode the moments of the estimate \(\hat\phi\) and the true phi:

\[ A = |\hat\phi|^2, \qquad B = \mathrm{Re}\, \hat\phi\, \phi^*, \qquad D = |\phi|^2 . \]

The merge averages them over realizations before taking the ratio

\[ r^2 = \frac{\langle B \rangle^2}{\langle A \rangle \langle D \rangle}, \qquad N_\phi = C_\phi \left( \frac{1}{r^2} - 1 \right), \]

with a delete-one-realization jackknife error.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
bash measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise.sh          #one job per seed
#copy map_joint_phi_noise_output/ to your machine, then
python measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/merge_map_joint_phi_noise.py --noise_dir <map_joint_phi_noise_output>

Settings at the top of the driver: nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, pol (I, P or IP: the data map_joint reconstructs phi from; default I), map_joint_steps, num_realizations, seed_prefix, out_dir_name (the output folder's name inside get_map_joint_phi_noise/, default map_joint_phi_noise_output). Each is a default that can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value>, e.g.

bash measure_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise.sh --noise_level=10 --out_dir_name=map_joint_phi_noise_output_10uk

A misspelled name is ignored and the default used. Each run writes the submission date and every setting to submission_settings.txt in the output folder (replacing any earlier copy); use a new out_dir_name when you change settings.

docs.title: Output: map_joint_phi_noise.npz
docs.text:
Key Content nphi per-mode phi noise on the rfft2 grid; NaN where the mean cross is <= 0, 0 at the origin nphi_error jackknife error nphi_leave_one_out the N leave-one-out nphi the jackknife comes from, shape (n_realizations, nside, nside // 2 + 1) box / cosmology keys nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, pol, param_names, params

Can be used in forecasting via fisher_forecast --delensed_covariance <npz> --phi_noise map_joint_phi_noise.npz (with the matching --pol) or as the noise source for the delensed covariance. Its spectra are plotted by measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_analysis.py (see Sampler Phi Noise).

docs.title: Sampler Phi Noise
docs.text:
Measures the phi reconstruction noise reached by the sampler's own posterior mean. Several chains per realization sample (f, phi) | d with theta held at GROUND_TRUTH (sample_joint's Gibbs sweep minus the theta step, fixed_theta_chain.posterior_mixed_draws). Chain 0 of each realization starts at phi = 0 and every other chain at its own draw from the \(C^{\phi\phi}\) prior, so the chains start far apart. Every phi sample is stored.

The merge burns every chain in and pools each realization's chains into its posterior mean \(\bar\phi\). Per mode, with the averages taken over realizations before the ratio,

\[ r^2 = \frac{\langle \mathrm{Re}(\bar\phi\,\phi_{\rm true}^*)\rangle}{\langle|\phi_{\rm true}|^2\rangle}, \qquad N = C^{\phi\phi}\left(\frac{1}{r^2} - 1\right). \]

This is the posterior mean's response to the truth. For the exact posterior mean it equals the squared correlation \(\langle \mathrm{Re}(\bar\phi\,\phi_{\rm true}^*)\rangle^2 / (\langle|\bar\phi|^2\rangle\langle|\phi_{\rm true}|^2\rangle)\) used for the map_joint phi noise, but it never uses \(\langle|\bar\phi|^2\rangle\), which the Monte Carlo error of a finite chain inflates. It is not valid for a MAP estimate, so map_joint keeps the correlation estimator.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
nohup bash measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise.sh > submit.log 2>&1 &   #num_maps x num_chains jobs
cd measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise
sbatch merge_sampler_phi_noise.sh --burn_in=600                          #default burn_in 300
python plot_sampler_convergence.py --merged sampler_phi_noise_output/sampler_phi_noise.npz

The driver submits through the submission throttle, so it keeps running until every job is submitted.

Its settings (nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, pol (I, P or IP: the data the chains sample from; default I), hmc_step_size, hmc_num_steps, num_sweeps, num_maps, seed_prefix, num_chains, chain_time, chain_mem, and out_dir_name, the output folder's name inside get_sampler_phi_noise/, default sampler_phi_noise_output) are defaults that can be overridden on the command line as --<name>=<value>, e.g.

bash measure_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise.sh --noise_level=10 --num_chains=4 --out_dir_name=sampler_phi_noise_output_10uk

A misspelled name is ignored and the default used. Each run writes the submission date and every setting to submission_settings.txt in the output folder (replacing any earlier copy); use a new out_dir_name when you change settings.

Each chain's random numbers come from its chain seed. --chain_seeds="11 22" gives chain 0 of every map the seed 11, chain 1 the seed 22, and so on; a chain with no seed listed (the default, chain_seeds empty) draws a random one, as sample_joint does. Either way the seed is saved as chain_seed in the chain's sidecar sampler_phi_NNNN_cK.npz, and rerunning with it reproduces the chain exactly. Give the chains of one map different seeds: two chains with the same seed would be identical.

The merge takes the same kind of overrides after the script name, burn_in (default 300) and out_dir_name (the driver's, default sampler_phi_noise_output):

sbatch merge_sampler_phi_noise.sh --burn_in=600 --out_dir_name=sampler_phi_noise_output_10uk

Each successful merge appends a line merged <date> by <user>: burn_in=<value> to that folder's submission_settings.txt, so the last such line describes the current sampler_phi_noise.npz.

The merge works on running jobs: each chain flushes its samples every 10 sweeps to a memory-mapped sampler_phi_NNNN_cK_samples.npy (realization NNNN, chain K), and the merge reads only the sweeps its sidecar sampler_phi_NNNN_cK.npz reports as done. A chain not yet past the burn-in is left out, and a realization's chains are trimmed to the shortest. Use rsync --sparse to copy a partial run.

Locally, for a small test:

python -m cmb_lensing.sampler_phi_noise --nside 64 --theta_pix 5 --n_maps 4 --n_chains 2 --n_sweeps 400 --burn_in 100 --out_dir <dir>

docs.title: Checking the burn-in
docs.text: plot_sampler_convergence.py writes sampler_rhat_<noise>uk.png next to the merged file. For each map it computes the Gelman-Rubin \(\hat R\) across that map's chains for the real and imaginary part of every Fourier mode, averages it over each \(|L|\) band, and plots the mean over maps with \(\pm 1\) standard deviation over maps as error bars. Every band near 1 (below the 1.01 reference line) means the chains agree after the burn-in; a band well above 1 means the burn-in or the chain length was too short there.

docs.title: Output: sampler_phi_noise.npz
docs.text: nphi (NaN where unmeasured, 0 at the origin), nphi_error, the N leave-one-out nphi_leave_one_out, rhat_real / rhat_imaginary (per map and mode), cphi, the mean moments, burn_in, n_chains, n_used, the seeds and the box / cosmology keys (including pol). Can be used for forecasting via fisher_forecast --delensed_covariance <npz> --phi_noise sampler_phi_noise.npz (with the matching --pol) or as the phi_noise key in the delensed covariance slurm script.

docs.title: Plotting the phi noise spectra
docs.text:
python measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_analysis.py

draws the merged map_joint_phi_noise.npz and sampler_phi_noise.npz (paths and box set in its __main__) against CAMB's \(C_L^{\phi\phi}\) and the box QE noise, into measure_phi_noise/phi_noise_plots/noise_level_<noise>uk/: phi_noise_spectra_<noise>uk.png (band medians) and phi_noise_spectra_over_qe_<noise>uk.png (band median of the ratio to the lensed-filter QE, with a jackknife band).
